title: Constraint Propagation and Score Stitching — internal notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures an internal sketch for how constraints should flow through the policy evaluation engine, how per-node scores are stitched into a single routing decision, and what explainability/audit logs we keep for post-hoc analysis. It focuses on multi-region control-plane interactions and pragmatic runtime constraints we need to meet for SLOs.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic, low-latency decisions for routing requests to model variants or regions while respecting hard constraints (compliance, data residency) and soft constraints (latency, cost).
- Produce an explainability trace for every routed decision that is small, redaction-safe, and sufficient for debugging/regression analysis.
- Ensure multi-region control plane remains eventual-consistent without violating hard constraints during rollouts or region failover.

Key concepts / terminology (how I use words here):
- local constraint: per-instance or per-region hard rule (e.g., "no PII leaves eu-west-1").
- global constraint: cluster-wide constraint (e.g., customer SLA min-throughput or blacklisted models).
- score vector: numeric affinities computed per candidate route (latency_score, cost_score, quality_score, freshness_score).
- score stitching: deterministic aggregation/ordering of score vectors from multiple evaluators into a single rank/choice.
- explainability bloom: compact sparse encoding of which constraints triggered and the top contributing score deltas (for traceability).

Design sketch: constraint propagation pipeline
1) Request enrichment (edge): collect request metadata (customer id, region hint, feature flags, auth context). Attach a short request-id and privacy-class tag (public/internal/PII).
2) Hard constraint sieve (edge/region): fast local checks that can short-circuit routing (e.g., data-residency block, customer-level denylist). This must be in the hot path and return boolean + blocking reason code.
3) Candidate enumeration (control-plane or local cache): a lightweight candidate set is produced (region/model variant pairs). Candidates should be pruned aggressively by cached hard constraints and by last-known capacity windows (stale-tolerant for up to 30s).
4) Scoring evaluators (distributed): each candidate is passed through a pipeline of independent scoring evaluators:
   - latency estimator (based on telemetry histograms, per-model kernel profiles, current queue length)
   - cost estimator (token-cost projection, GPU instance multipliers)
   - quality predictor (cheap model of recent evals per-prompt-class; returns expected quality delta)
   - compliance risk scorer (binary-to-penalty mapping for potential policy violations)
   - freshness penalty (age of model binary, KV cache hit probability)
   - experimental weight overrides (can be zeroed for stable tier)
Each evaluator returns a scalar in a pre-defined range and an optional short reason.

Score stitching and normalization
- Canonical vector shape: [latency_ms_est, cost_usd_est, quality_score, compliance_penalty, freshness_penalty, experimental_bonus]. All values normalized to a common 0-1 scale at the evaluator boundary.
- Stitcher responsibilities:
  1) Validate shape and fill missing values with safe defaults (e.g., unknown quality -> 0.5).
  2) Apply per-customer or per-route weight vector (configurable via control plane).
  3) Compute a composite score S = w_latency * f(latency) + w_cost * f(cost) + w_quality * quality_score - w_compliance * compliance_penalty + w_experimental * experimental_bonus. f(latency) maps ms -> 0..1 via invertible monotonic transform.
  4) For tie-breaking, use deterministic stable keys: (composite_score, freshness_penalty, region_preference_rank, candidate_id).
- Important: all transforms and weights are part of the control-plane config with semantic versioning. When weights change during rollout, we tag decisions with the policy_version and store the previous policy_version in the trace.

Explainability logs (what to record and why)
Constraints: small, redaction-safe, privacy-preserving. We must avoid logging customer prompt text; log only indices and coarse prompt-class fingerprints.
Minimum explain payload per decision (compact JSON-like):
- request_id, decision_timestamp, policy_version (string), chosen_candidate_id, composite_score, score_vector (6 floats), top_3_contributors (list of "name:delta" strings), hard_block_reasons (if any), sampling_flag.
- If sampling_flag==true (1% by default), include expanded context: evaluator_versions, raw latency_histogram_snapshot (coarse buckets), region_capacity_snapshot, small hashed prompt fingerprint.
Retention and access:
- Full traces (sampling_flag) persisted for 90 days in encrypted object storage.
- Minimum explain payload persisted for 365 days in compressed event-store for audits.
- Access logged via KMS-protected audit flow and requires two-person review for customer-level traces.

Multi-region control-plane considerations
Control-plane model: hybrid leaderless config with tombstones for deleted configs. Key ideas:
- Policy configs are stored in S3-like storage + Raft-backed region index for low-latency reads. We push configs to regional caches with a TTL and a signed config digest.
- Versioning: every policy has a monotonic policy_version string + semantic fields. Control-plane provides a small "delta" apply mechanism (patch sets) so regional caches can apply minimal diffs.
- Staleness window: we allow region caches to be stale for up to 60s for non-critical fields (experimental weights), but hard constraints (data residency, denylists) are tagged MUST_APPLY and are applied immediately via a secondary invalidation bus (pub/sub).
- During region failover: local hard constraint checks still apply. For failover routing we prefer warm standby region candidates that have seen the most recent MUST_APPLY tombstones. If a MUST_APPLY conflict exists (region cache says allow, central says deny), central policy wins and regional caches are quarantined until invalidation is acknowledged.

Performance & operational heuristics
- Hot path must do at most one RPC to local cache; avoid synchronous control-plane lookups.
- Stitcher compute budget: target 150us median. We allow 95th up to 2ms, but that must be exceptional.
- Sampling budget for full traces: dynamic rate based on error budget and anomaly scores (if composite_score deviates > X from historical median).
- Perf experiment: evaluate a micro-stitcher inside the serving process (C++) vs a separate microservice (Go). Tradeoffs: latency vs deployability.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to encode cascading constraints where a global constraint modifies the interpretation of local constraints (e.g., global high-load => allow relaxed residency for non-PII traffic)? Need formal predicate algebra.
- Policy testing harness: design a small fuzzing harness that generates request shapes and validates policy monotonicity across version rollouts.
- Quantify cost of storing score vectors at full volume (10M req/day) — compression and integer packing required.
- Decide retention window tradeoffs for sampled traces vs compliance obligations per region (EU vs US).

Implementation notes & immediate action items
- Prototype: implement score vector struct + stitcher in a single binary inside the runtime (C++). Feature flags to toggle remote-stitcher call. (Owner: Ravi)
- Small RFC to add MUST_APPLY bit to policy config schema and invalidation bus semantics. (Owner: Denise)
- Add unit tests for tie-break determinism and policy_version tagging. (Owner: Tom)

References and context links:
- Confluence page with policy data model: CONFLUENCE-1234
- GitHub PR with initial stitcher impl: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-eval/pull/412
- JIRA epic for policy multi-region work: JIRA-PI-879

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Keep explainability bloom tiny; prefer top-3 contributor deltas over full evaluator traces except for sampled cases.
- Treat compliance_penalty as a multiplier that can veto a candidate when > 0.9.
- Policy changes must be backwards-readable for 30 days to support rollbacks.
